title: Correct schedule step selection before extending model support
description: The real hook probe in research/run_anima_emphasis.py reproduces an existing index-scaling error with equal sampler/prepared counts: 2 steps expected [0,1], observed [0,0]; 3 expected [0,1,2], observed [0,1,1]; 6 duplicates step 2 and skips final embedding; 30 duplicates index14 and never selects29. Formula round(raw_step*(N-1)/actual_steps) is responsible. Retain the failed probe, independently define integer/fractional schedule semantics, correct index mapping, and add tests that assert prompt selection rather than repeat the formula. This is separate from Anima preprocessing/metadata constraints.

title: Switch or explicitly constrain SDXL pooled conditioning during schedules
description: Review of encoder extraction found a pre-existing schedule limitation: hooks.py consumes target_cond but ignores target_pooled, and the base metadata pins pooled_output to the first prompt. Token embeddings change while SDXL pooled conditioning stays fixed. This behavior is documented in README, encoding/base.py and encoding/README.md. Design the swap at the model-conditioning boundary or explicitly reject incompatible pooled changes; add an independent SDXL sampler-level regression without assuming raw pooled vectors can be swapped after model-specific preprocessing. Review artifact: /tmp/review-mcp-run-6mky28f0.

title: Qualify opt-in Anima emphasis candidates before production integration
description: Research in ANIMA_EMPHASIS_FINDINGS.md demonstrates native neutral-syntax token changes and a single-pass candidate with identity at weight1 across 14 artist/concept cases. Anima key RMS normalization largely cancels positive key scaling; values retain it. Temporary log-weight attention bias is CFG-tested and rendered for two artist prompts. RMS normalization is an independent candidate; mean-preserving scaling flipped sign once and reached ~6x. Before adding production options, broaden prompts/checkpoints/seeds, preserve native mode, qualify partial-token spans and exact user-facing strength semantics, and decide model-aware wiring for downstream attention control. One AnimaYume checkpoint/seed does not establish style quality or SDXL-equivalent strengths.
notes: Five fixed seeds on supplied SilvermoonMix v23 prompt: cutesexyrobutts singlepass3 signatures5/5 vs attention-bias3 zero detected0/5; other2 artists no detected signatures in either mode. Bias retains visible style/rendering shifts, typically subtler. Mode integration now completed in sxu at user request, native default. Wider qualification remains open: matched perceived strength, more checkpoints/prompts and practical low-weight calibration; do not infer equal-style-strength superiority. Evidence research/SILVERMOON_MULTISEED_FINDINGS.md and hashed visual_assessment.json.

title: Design Anima conditioning semantics before enabling segmentation and schedules
description: The encoding package now preserves native static Anima metadata and declares BREAK, scheduling/alternation and normalization unsupported. A previous experiment concatenated independently encoded Qwen fragments and T5 IDs before the adapter; it proved tensor preservation but not end-to-end isolation and has been removed. Define whether segmentation is useful at all for this LLM/adapter path before enabling it. Existing hooks.py swaps raw c_crossattn after Anima.extra_conds has transformed Qwen conditioning using T5 IDs/weights, so schedules need a preprocessing-aware design. Define normalization at the correct boundary and validate with the actual model/sampler before enabling. Inherited Qwen fragment tokenization remains a separate behavior decision.
